backups.WARNING: 184935 and 185109 contain CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `leader`; USE `leader`; - restoring them into ANY target database will overwrite `leader`. Any future restore test must strip those lines or use a dump made without --databases.

incident_summary: Between 21:49:42 and 21:55:21 five restore-verification runs of a mysqldump that contained CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `leader`; USE `leader`; executed DROP TABLE/CREATE TABLE/INSERT against `leader` itself (threads 219, 222, 225, 226, 228), each stopped mid-run. companies and company_invoices were left dropped; containers and model_has_roles were left empty. Manual recovery (threads 230, 234) and the leader<-leader_dryrun sync (thread 237) restored them. Net data effect: zero (proven row-level).
recommended_recovery_action: OPTION 1 (recommended): Owner approves a targeted schema correction of the 7 divergent definitions so leader matches the approved clone exactly (DROP + re-ADD of 5 FKs without ON DELETE clause; RENAME INDEX for 2 UNIQUE keys), executed with the same guards (identity, write-free, backup), then the full postflight. Data restore is NOT needed.

OPTION 2: Owner instead approves the CURRENT leader definitions as the target (CASCADE on 3 FKs matches historical migrations; CASCADE on 2 receipts FKs matches neither migrations (SET NULL) nor clone (NO ACTION)) and re-baselines the clone; this changes delete semantics on financial tables and needs explicit business sign-off.

OPTION 3: Owner orders full rollback of leader to backup 184935 (data identical to current, so this only removes all constraints) followed by a clean single-pass re-execution of the unmodified approved runner. Highest effort, no data benefit.
In all options: before any further restore test, strip CREATE DATABASE/USE from dumps or dump without --databases.
